title: Israel Election Ends Without a Clear Majority as Netanyahu and Eisenkot Blocs Fall Short
dek: Early counts put Netanyahu's bloc near 54 seats and the opposition near 47 in the 120-seat Knesset, leaving neither side within reach of 61 and putting Arab parties in the middle of coalition arithmetic.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Ballot papers from Israel's 2019 legislative election

keyPoints: CNN reported projections of about 54 seats for Netanyahu's bloc and 47 for the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot, short of the 61 needed for a majority in the 120-seat Knesset.
The Jerusalem Post reported final turnout of 77.7% when polls closed, up 7.1 points from 2022, per the Central Elections Committee.
Arab parties rose to about 18 seats, according to the Jerusalem Post, making them central to any government that opposes Netanyahu.
Official results are expected by the end of Wednesday, but coalition talks could take several days or longer.
body:
Israel's election closed with no clear winner. Early vote counts and exit polls showed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc and the opposition led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot both falling short of the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat Knesset.

## Where the count stands

With more than 70 percent of the vote counted, CNN reported that Netanyahu's bloc was projected to take 54 seats, down from the 68-seat coalition he led in the outgoing Knesset. Likud is still expected to be the largest single party. The opposition bloc was projected at 47 seats. The Jerusalem Post, reporting after more than 4 million votes were counted, gave the same picture: Netanyahu's bloc at 54 and the opposition at 47.

The Central Elections Committee reported final turnout of 77.7% when polling stations closed at 10 p.m., up 7.1 percentage points from the 2022 election, according to the Jerusalem Post. Earlier on Tuesday, turnout had been running at a record pace: 55.7% of eligible voters had voted by 4 p.m. local time, the highest figure recorded by that hour since 1973, according to figures reported by the Times of Israel.

## Arab parties and the path to a majority

Parties opposed to Netanyahu hold a combined lead in the projections, at about 65 seats according to CNN, but they are split across right, left and center. CNN reported that they would likely need to work with the Arab parties to oust him. The Jerusalem Post reported that Arab parties rose to about 18 seats, and that the Joint List celebrated a seat gain.

In a speech to supporters at Likud headquarters after the first exit polls, Netanyahu called for a "strong, right-wing" government and warned against relying on Arab parties, according to the Associated Press and the Jerusalem Post. The Jerusalem Post also reported Trump's claim that his endorsement of Netanyahu had shifted momentum toward the prime minister. Those are claims by the leaders involved, not confirmed results.

## What happens next

Israel's parliamentary system requires a governing majority in the Knesset, usually assembled through coalition talks after the count is final. CNN reported that finalizing the tally could take several days, and seat projections can still move until then. The Associated Press described Netanyahu as far from defeated, while noting that neither bloc won a majority in the exit polls.

The result matters beyond Israel's borders. The next coalition will shape Israeli policy on Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, and its relationship with Washington.
